item.title: Rachel Roddy’s recipe for figs with raspberry cream and cat tongue biscuits | A kitchen in Rome
item.summary: Combine these simple Italian baked treats with chilled fruit and thick cream for a playful summer pudding In his exquisite The French Menu Cookbook , Richard Olney has clear ideas and strong opinions about everything, including dessert. He believed that rich desserts should follow only the simplest of meals, whereas with most menus (meaning all the sophisticated menus in his book), something light, airy and playful is best. His suggestions read like a summer fruit poem: peach melba, apple mousse with peaches, apricot fritters dusted with icing sugar, strawberries in sweetened orange juice, strawberries in beaujolais, strawberry mousse with raspberry puree, iced cherries and fresh almonds. One of his late summer/early autumn menus also suggests fresh figs with raspberry cream ( figues à la crème framboise ), which is both fun to make (the red puree streaking through the cream for a raspberry ripple) and to eat. An airy and playful pudding calls for an airy and playful biscuit. What better than lingue di gatto, or cat tongues, so called because of their flat, elongated shape.
